original.target_description: Efficiency relative to first-best equilibrium, money versus no-money environments; two population-size-specific Mann-Whitney tests located, target contrast unresolved.

n.sample_role: Candidate analytic units: session-level efficiency ratios; 9 sessions for M6/NM6 or 8 sessions for M14/NM14, not assigned.
n.exclusions: All-period session averages used in the located comparisons; additional exclusions not described. Target contrast unresolved.
n.location: Author manuscript pp. 18, 26–27; Tables 7 and 12; Finding 7 efficiency comparison
n.quote:
Nevertheless, using the session-level eﬃciency ratios over all rounds as reported in
Table 7 for the money treatment sessions and in the last three columns of Table 12 for the no
money treatment sessions, a Wilcoxon Mann-Whitney test indicates that we can reject the
null hypothesis of no diﬀerence in eﬃciency ratios between 1) the M6 and NM6 treatments
and 2) the M14 and NM14 treatments in favor of the alternative that eﬃciency ratios are
higher in each of the two M treatments relative to the comparable NM treatment ( = 01
for the first test and  = 04 for the second test).

notes: Identity: supplied canonical text begins with the source URL https://sites.socsci.uci.edu/~duffy/papers/lw_exp_final.pdf and DOI 10.1257/aer.104.6.1735; title Gift Exchange versus Monetary Exchange: Theory and Evidence; John Duﬀy and Daniela Puzzello; dated September 20, 2013. This is a full author manuscript with methods, results, tables and appendices, matching the authors/title/project of the neutral AER reference, but predating the 2014 publication. Published pagination/version equivalence is not independently established. No PDF was supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. Tables 7 and 12 identify efficiency relative to the first-best equilibrium. Their comparison supports two distinct critical tests: M6 versus NM6 and M14 versus NM14. The neutral description and study identifier do not specify population size or pooling. Cannot select either test or combine them by row order or numeric matching. Printed candidates: efficiency all-period means M6 0.43 and NM6 0.27, M14 0.31 and NM14 0.21; these are separate group means, not a printed mean difference. The text reports exact Mann-Whitney p=.01 for M6 versus NM6 and p=.04 for M14 versus NM14 (same efficiency outcome), with session-level observations. Candidate analytic counts from final session rows in Tables 7 and 12: M6 sessions 1–4 (4) plus NM6 sessions 9–13 (5), 4 + 5 = 9 sessions; M14 sessions 5–8 (4) plus NM14 sessions 14–17 (4), 4 + 4 = 8 sessions. These are mutually exclusive session groups, not participant counts; no additional session exclusions are described in the cited comparison. Counts remain candidates because the assigned target contrast is ambiguous. No effect-size subtraction or conversion performed. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only.
